title: Politeness & Etiquette
description: Learn how to say yes, no, sorry, please, and express that you don't understand in colloquial Tamil.

exercises.question: How do you say 'sorry / excuse me' in colloquial Tamil?
exercises.explanation: 'Mannikkanum' is the colloquial Tamil way to say sorry or excuse me. It literally means 'need to forgive'.
These four words are essential for everyday polite conversation in Tamil.
'Purila' is the short colloquial form of 'I don't understand' in everyday Tamil speech.

exercises.question: What does 'aamaa' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Aamaa' means yes in Tamil — used in both casual and polite conversations.
Say 'mannikkanum' (sorry) then 'enakku purila' (I don't understand) when you need clarification.
'Medhuvaa pesunga' = please speak slowly — medhuvaa = slowly, pesunga = please speak (polite).
'Medhuvaa pesunga' — medhuvaa (slowly) comes before pesunga (please speak).
'Illai' is the Tamil word for no — also used as a negator in sentences.
